# LittleTidy 0.8.2
- Fixed: permanent deletion no longer stops halfway when a folder contains files owned by another user (such as root, or an account that no longer exists) or locked files. LittleTidy now checks first and moves such folders to the Trash instead, explaining why; Finder asks for an administrator password when you empty the Trash. This affected, for example, downloaded Codex updates and some Xcode build folders.
Requires macOS 26 or later.

# LittleTidy 0.8.1
- Temporary folders of closed Claude sessions (screenshots, videos, builds, and scratch files) are now offered for cleanup, one item per session. Running sessions are never offered, and each session is checked again right before cleanup. Conversation transcripts are kept. - Codex and Antigravity caches, including downloaded app updates, are now recognized. AI app caches are cleaned only when no app has files open inside them. - Simulator devices now include the OS version in their name, so the same model on two runtimes no longer looks duplicated. - Empty items, such as XCTest clones whose folder is already gone, are no longer preselected. - The Overview total no longer counts space that Simulator clones share with their source device. - Developer Storage scans finish sooner: the Homebrew estimate runs alongside the rest of the scan.
Requires macOS 26 or later.

# LittleTidy 0.8.0
- XCTest clones that Xcode creates for parallel testing are now recommended for cleanup and removed with `simctl`. While a test run is active, every clone is protected until it finishes. - Developer cleanup no longer stops entirely while Xcode is open. Build data of projects that are not open, and Simulator devices nothing is using, can be cleaned; everything else Xcode owns waits until you quit it. Derived Data is now listed per project. - Sizes now show how much space is freed right away. Simulator clones share storage, and a Time Machine local snapshot keeps older data until macOS releases it, so the app shows "at least X freed right away" and explains when a snapshot is holding space. - After a cleanup, you can ask macOS to release the space a local snapshot still holds. macOS removes local snapshots, oldest first, until that space is reclaimed; backups on a Time Machine disk are not affected. - Old Homebrew versions and downloads are estimated with `brew cleanup --dry-run` and reclaimed with `brew cleanup`. - Cleanup results show the total removed, the measured change in free space, what is still in the Trash, and the reason for every skipped or failed item. Removed items leave the list immediately. - Fixed: the deletion mode chosen in Settings now applies without relaunching, and is no longer overwritten by the previous value. Cleanup wording now matches permanent-delete mode. - Fixed: symbolic links, such as `~/.swiftpm/cache`, are no longer offered for cleanup.
Requires macOS 26 or later. Releasing snapshot space removes local hourly restore points and cannot be undone. Homebrew cleanup requires Homebrew in `/opt/homebrew` or `/usr/local`.
